146197.why:
What I did: typed ZZLONGROW into search and opened the Work orders tab.
What I saw: both rows cut the bold first line short with a “…”. The row reads “S2-34379 ZZLONGROW Heavy Haulage And Trailer Repair Services …” and hides “Of Greater Fernvale 123786”. The work order number and the word I typed are both still readable on the row.
Why that is a fail: this case says a value cut short with “...” is a fail.
How I know it is not my screen: I measured at four screen widths from 1280 up to 2560 and the search panel is a fixed 640px every time, so the cut is identical on every screen. A picture of the row shows the “…” painted on screen, which agrees with the measurement.

146198.why:
What I did: the word this case tells you to type, ZZLONGROW, sits at the START of the name, where a cut from the right can never reach it — so typing it makes this case pass no matter how badly the row is cut. This case’s own BEFORE YOU START asks for a match near the END of the value, so I typed Fernvale, which sits in the part of these same records that gets cut off. The Expected Results were not changed.
What I saw: work orders S2-34379 and S2-34376 come back, and the word Fernvale is nowhere on either row. The cut removes it completely. The row comes back and cannot say why.
How I know the search panel can show it: two other rows in the very same list, S2-34360 and S2-34157, do show Fernvale highlighted. So these two rows are genuinely hiding it.
Also worth fixing in this case itself: the word it tells the tester to type cannot show the problem it is looking for. A change to BEFORE YOU START is proposed separately.

146199.why: Typed ZZLONGROW, opened the Work orders tab. The whole line is there and the typed word is marked inside it — the marking sits on top of the text, it does not replace it. Taking the marked and unmarked pieces together gives back the complete line with no character lost.

146202.why:
This case is HELD by its own Expected Results: “THIS CASE IS HELD: the specification does not say what should happen here. Do not pass or fail it. Record what you saw.” So it is recorded as Blocked, not as a pass or a fail, and what follows is only what was seen.

What I did: typed “SVEWU82M5ETEJFWFA” into search and opened the Work orders tab.
What I saw: Typed the VIN. 20 work orders come back, and every row says why: the second line ends with “VIN: SVEWU82M5ETEJFWFA” and the typed value is highlighted there. So on this build the row does explain itself for this field.

What this is waiting on: a decision on whether a row must say which field the match came from. Until that is answered this case cannot be judged either way.
